full_judgment:
"I do hereby authorise my husband Mr. AFM Naziruddin, Manager, Loan Department of your Bank to construct a building on my plot of land bearing No. 175 (New), Elephant Road, Dhaka, Mouza Dhaninondi, under JL No. 724 (part) old and new No. 2053 (part) and I have no objection if any loan is sanctioned disbursed for this purpose. Further, I declare that I have mortgaged the said property in favour of IDBP and executed the required document." 

 The Chief Manager, 

 17. According to Mr. Ahmed, the learned Advocate for the respondent this is the licence given by the appellant to the respondent to construct a building on the suit land. According to Mr. MH Khandker, the learned Advocate for the appellant, Ext. 1 is not a licence neither in form nor in essence but the same is a mere letter of authority for raising loan from the Shilpa Bank for which the appellant had already mortgaged her land of schedule 'A' to the Bank by executing the required document. Mr. Khandker has drawn our attention to the bye-laws regarding House Building Advance by IDBP, Ext. 3, wherefrom it will appear that a House Building Advance to a confirmed employee of the Bank can be sanctioned "for construction of a house on a land already in his possession or in possession of his wife" provided of course the other conditions are satisfied. In Ext. 1 it has been mentioned" to construct a building on my plot of land." Mr. Khandker has rightly contended that the document is to be construed as a whole and reading Ext. 1 along with bye-laws it would be apparent that by no stretch of imagination Ext. 1 could be regarded as a licence granted by the appellant to the respondent. This document was addressed to the Chief Officer, Central Accounts Department, IDBP, Head Office, Dhaka, by the appellant authorising her husband to take loan from IDBP and it further shows that the land described in schedule 'A' had already been mortgaged by the appellant in favour of the IDBP by executing the required documents as security for the purpose of obtaining the loan. It may be pointed out that according to the bye-laws the employee shall be bound by the other clauses for payment of the House Building Advances and he will not be entitled to withdraw his Provident Fund and Gratuity until the House Building loan with interest is realised. Upon a true and correct construction of the letter of authority, Ext. 1 we are of the opinion that the same is not a licence granted by the appellant in favour of the respondent for construction of the suit building. We, therefore, hold that the learned Subordinate Judge was wrong in presuming that Ext. 1 is a licence to the respondent for construction of the suit building on the suit land granted by the appellant. Since we held that Ext. 1 is not a licence the question of its admissibility in evidence does not arise.
